newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cricket-Law slams 144 as Queensland take charge.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-Law slams 144 as Queensland take charge.

text.p: Discarded Australia limited overs batsman Stuart Law hit a dashing 144 on Friday as Queensland moved into a dominant position on the second day of their four-day Sheffield Shield match against New South Wales.
Law's innings helped Shield leaders Queensland to 460 for six at stumps at the Gabba ground, a lead of 270 on New South Wales' meagre first innings of 190 all out.
Law was dropped last week from the Australia side for the World Series limited overs competition and hit back at national selectors with his 22nd first-class century.
Law and number three batsman Jimmy Maher put on a partnership of 244 for the third wicket, a record against New South Wales, after Queensland had been 41 for two.
Maher fell for 91 to a sharp catch at leg slip by Steve Waugh from the bowling of Australia team mate Michael Bevan.
Waugh then took the catch to dismiss Law from the bowling of test paceman Glenn McGrath.
England-born all-rounder Andrew Symonds hit a typically quick 50, while Australia wicketkeeper Ian Healy enforced his side's dominance even more and was 82 not out at stumps.
Healy's innings came after his 161 not out in the first test against West Indies last month to give him an average of 288 at the ground this season.
In Perth, South Australia struggled to 231 for eight at stumps on the first day of their match against Western Australia.

South Australia were in trouble at 36 for two after captain Jamie Siddons won the toss and elected to bat. Siddons was made to regret his decision when he fell to Australia limited overs all-rounder Tom Moody for a duck.
Darren Lehmann and James Brayshaw steered their side out of trouble with half-centuries, Brayshaw making 73 and Lehmann 52.
